re_line: DPRK SRBM launch (2nd consecutive day) · KOSPI -5.1% on Hormuz tensions · SK Hynix 54.3T won fab investment · ROK-US new envoy meeting · polysilicon tariff 15%
morning_memo: North Korea launched a second consecutive short-range ballistic missile toward the East Sea on Aug 6, with state media silent on both launches — KCNA blackout on missile tests has occurred in the Aug 6 and Aug 7 reporting cycle as Ulchi Freedom Shield approaches.
KOSPI fell 5.1% on Aug 7 for a second straight session, driven by foreign selling amid renewed Strait of Hormuz tensions, reversing a portion of the record 18% single-day surge recorded July 31.
SK Hynix announced 54.3 trillion won in combined domestic fab investment — Yongin Y2 and Cheongju M17 — the largest single domestic capital commitment announcement in today's feed.

key_stat.label: SK Hynix domestic fab investment — Yongin Y2 + Cheongju M17
key_stat.context: Announced Aug 7, the combined Yongin Y2 and Cheongju M17 commitment represents the largest single domestic semiconductor capital outlay in today's feed, underscoring the AI chip-driven investment cycle even as KOSPI fell 5.1% on Hormuz-related selling.
key_stat.source: Yonhap English — SK hynix to invest 54.3 tln won in Yongin's Y2 fab, Cheongju's M17 fab

imagery_report.label: Flooding destroys DPRK military base near border; parade training stands down
imagery_report.headline: Planet Labs imagery confirms 380+ homes destroyed at North Korean military base near border; NK Pro satellite analysis also shows parade training trucks dispersed after small July event
imagery_report.body: NK Pro analysis of Planet Labs imagery shows at least 380 duplex-style single-story homes were completely washed away at a North Korean military base close to the South Korean border after a dam appeared to break in late July. Separately, NK Pro satellite imagery analysis shows hundreds of transport trucks used for soldier transport at North Korea's main military parade training base have disappeared following a small-scale parade late last month, indicating no large-scale parade is planned in the near term. The flood damage at the border-adjacent base adds a new humanitarian and operational variable to DPRK military readiness assessments ahead of Ulchi Freedom Shield.

source_links.label: NK Pro — Flooding wipes out North Korean villages at key military base near border
NK Pro — North Korean military parade training ends after small July event, imagery shows

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: 38 North published analysis Jul 16 of North Korea's expanding uranium and conventional missile production, consistent with Kim Jong Un's formal July 11-12 directive to expand nuclear forces 'both in quality and quantity.' Apr 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: 38 North published analysis Jul 31 on what Choe Hyon destroyer reveals about North Korea's maritime strategy. Jun 30, 2026: NK Pro satellite imagery shows the Choe Hyon destroyer, commissioned June 25 by Kim Jong Un, remains docked at a west coast civilian cargo port one week after KCNA claimed it departed for operations. NK Pro also uncovered previously unreported details about where a test of its sister ship (Kang Kon) was conducted on the east coast. Feb 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after 2+ years of fitting-out but still not operational as of May 2025. New submarine construction begun in separate bay.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site — Seongju County
bp_locations.note: Jun 21, 2026: All six THAAD launchers returned to the permanent Seongju site from Osan Air Base, restoring the battery's full deployment footprint. Battery operational status remains subject to ongoing assessment after the partial Middle East redeployment.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: NK Pro satellite imagery analysis published Jul 21 shows North Korea has begun fixing up the surface of the coastal launchpad at Sohae, assessed as the latest sign of preparation to resume military spy satellite launches. Prior reports showed a 2,500 kN engine test stand firing and a new viewing area building nearing completion.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: A seismic event near North Korea's nuclear test site is being assessed by Yonhap as potentially related to a nuclear test (Aug 3, 2026). ROK MOU research reported July 31 that approximately 30% of North Korean defectors from areas near the Punggye-ri nuclear site show chromosomal mutations potentially linked to radiation exposure. Nov 2025: ROK DIA assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: New 38 North satellite imagery published Aug 6 shows Russian construction at the Tumen River vehicle bridge has made further progress toward an opening. Russia targets early September to open the bridge; the crossing is described as largely ready with finishing touches underway. Earlier 38 North analysis (Jul 1-3, 2026) assessed the opening as unlikely in the near term, citing incomplete customs infrastructure on both sides. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025; ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: Mar 12, 2026: Cross-border passenger train service resumed between Sinuiju and Dandong after COVID-era suspension. New Yalu River Bridge may open in 2026. NK Pro satellite imagery analysis published July 7, 2026 shows over a dozen makeshift smuggling routes across the NK-China border that went quiet since late 2025 have appeared active again in recent weeks.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: NK Pro analysis published Jul 17 shows North Korea has started a new construction project at the Rajin Shipyard in the Rason SEZ, with Planet Labs and Maxar imagery showing a likely construction worker camp built at the shipyard, following Kim Jong Un's call to build larger and more capable warships. Nov 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: NK Pro Planet Labs imagery (Aug 7) confirms at least 380 homes destroyed at a North Korean military base close to the South Korean border after a dam appeared to break in late July — flood damage adds operational uncertainty to DPRK forces near the NLL. Jul 12, 2026: A ROK Navy seaman apprentice went missing during an overnight East Sea patrol; the sailor's body was subsequently recovered. Sep 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed NLL near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south; ROK Navy fired ~60 warning shots.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of PMZ Jan 27-28, 2026 to Weihai shipyard following Lee Jae-myung Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai (Russian Far East)
bp_locations.note: Jan 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice — one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked Jan 14 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since Sep 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels delivered ~15,800 containers from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai.

rok_government.action: Lee designates Andong and 4 nearby towns as special disaster zones after heavy rains
rok_government.detail: President Lee Jae-myung designated the southeastern city of Andong and four nearby towns as special disaster zones following heavy rains and flooding. The designation unlocks emergency relief funding and expedited recovery assistance.

rok_government.action: Lee calls on generals to help restore public trust in military after martial law imposition
rok_government.detail: President Lee Jae-myung addressed military generals Friday, urging them to take active steps to rebuild public confidence in the armed forces following the martial law imposition under the previous administration. Lee also pledged to remedy damage caused by state violence.

rok_government.action: Defense ministry reaffirms commitment to swift integration of military academies
rok_government.detail: The Ministry of National Defense reaffirmed its commitment Friday to proceeding with the integration of the military academies, pushing back against a PPP-led National Assembly resolution calling for a halt to the process.

rok_government.action: National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac meets new US envoy Steel
rok_government.detail: National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac met with the new US envoy Steel, according to a ROK official, in the first recorded meeting between the two since Steel's arrival as the new American representative to Seoul.

rok_government.action: Unification advisers say using North Korea's official name is not new
rok_government.detail: A unification advisory council said Friday that North Korea's official name has been used in official contexts before, pushing back on controversy over the Lee administration's approach to nomenclature in inter-Korean policy documents.

rok_government.ministry: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy / Ministry of Environment
rok_government.action: Industry and climate ministries team up to promote battery recycling industry
rok_government.detail: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources and the climate ministry announced a joint initiative Friday to promote South Korea's battery recycling sector, targeting supply chain resilience for critical minerals used in EV batteries.

calendar_watch.headline: Korean Liberation Day (광복절) — Presidential Address
calendar_watch.detail: President Lee Jae-myung will deliver the annual Liberation Day address, traditionally watched for inter-Korean policy signals and tone-setting on DPRK engagement. The speech comes amid consecutive DPRK SRBM launches and Kim Yo Jong's warnings against Japan.

calendar_watch.headline: Ulchi Freedom Shield — US-ROK Combined Exercise (estimated start)
calendar_watch.detail: The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield combined military exercise is expected to begin in mid-August, typically running 11 days. DPRK has launched SRBMs on consecutive days (Aug 6-7) in what analysts assess as exercise run-up provocation activity.

calendar_watch.headline: DPRK Founding Day — 78th Anniversary
calendar_watch.detail: September 9 marks the 78th anniversary of the DPRK's founding. The date has historically been accompanied by military parades, missile tests, or major weapons demonstrations; watch for further provocations in the Aug-Sep window.

calendar_watch.headline: DPRK Workers' Party Founding Day
calendar_watch.detail: October 10 marks the DPRK Workers' Party founding anniversary, historically accompanied by military displays. Combined with the Sep 9 founding day, the Aug-Oct window is the peak provocation risk period for 2026.

calendar_watch.headline: Section 301 Investigation — USTR (Korea)
calendar_watch.detail: The USTR Section 301 investigation into South Korea (launched Mar 11, 2026) is ongoing with no announced deadline; following Section 122 surcharge expiry July 24, Section 301 is now the primary legal vehicle for potential new tariff authority against Korea.

rok_assembly.action: PPP lawmakers submit resolution calling for halt to military academy integration
rok_assembly.detail: Lawmakers from the People Power Party submitted a National Assembly resolution Friday calling on the government to stop proceeding with integration of the military academies, in direct opposition to the MND's reaffirmed commitment to the merger.

top_stories.headline: North Korea fires short-range ballistic missile toward East Sea — second consecutive day launch
top_stories.body: North Korea launched a short-range ballistic missile toward the East Sea on August 6, the second consecutive day of SRBM launches, per South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff. KCNA remained silent on both launches, a pattern the DPRK has used selectively in the past when testing audience management around sensitive dates. The launches come as Kim Jong Un has been absent from public view for 10 days and as the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise approaches in mid-August.
top_stories.so_what: Directly relevant to Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise posture and the Aug 15 Liberation Day presidential address signaling.
top_stories.pattern_note: CSIS provocations database records a North Korea SRBM launch on Aug 10, 2019 from near Hamhung — two short-range missiles fired — in a comparable pre-exercise provocation window.

top_stories.headline: SK Hynix announces 54.3 trillion won investment in Yongin Y2 and Cheongju M17 fabs
top_stories.body: SK Hynix said Friday it will invest a combined 54.3 trillion won across its Yongin Y2 and Cheongju M17 fabrication facilities, marking the largest single domestic semiconductor capital commitment in today's news cycle. The investment comes as South Korea's H1 exports overtook Japan's on AI chip demand, according to KED Global reporting.
top_stories.so_what: Affects the domestic semiconductor cluster buildout that ROK government is actively supporting, including ongoing discussions to ease the 52-hour workweek rule for the Gwangju semiconductor cluster.

top_stories.headline: KOSPI falls 5.1% for second straight session on foreign selling amid renewed Hormuz tensions
top_stories.body: Seoul shares ended lower for a second consecutive session Friday, with the KOSPI closing at 6,258.77 (down 5.1%), as foreign investors sold on renewed tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The two-day slide follows the record 18% single-day surge on July 31, and Brent crude fell 2.36% to $81.79 as the Hormuz situation remained fluid.
top_stories.so_what: Hormuz tension directly affects South Korea's energy import costs and export shipping routes; CSIS published analysis Aug 6 on the Hormuz implications for Korea's energy policymaking.

top_stories.headline: Trump imposes 15% tariff on polysilicon derivatives, driving rally in Hanwha and OCI shares
top_stories.body: President Trump imposed a 15% tariff on polysilicon derivatives, triggering a share rally for Korean solar material producers Hanwha and OCI, which benefit from protection against cheaper Chinese polysilicon exports to the US market. The tariff — at the same 15% rate as the US-Korea strategic deal baseline for certain goods — effectively penalizes Chinese producers competing with Korean-affiliated supply chains in the US solar sector.
top_stories.so_what: Affects the US-Korea strategic investment deal's energy and materials sector calculations and ROK manufacturers' positioning in the US solar supply chain.

overnight_items.headline: KCNA silent on Aug 6 SRBM launch — second consecutive blackout
overnight_items.body_text: North Korea's state media did not report on Thursday's short-range ballistic missile launch, marking a second consecutive blackout on DPRK missile tests. KCNA's silence on missile launches is selectively used; the pattern over the past week has paired Kim Yo Jong's written statements on Japan with operational launches unreported by state media. Kim Jong Un has now been absent from public view for 10 days.

overnight_items.headline: ROK National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac meets new US envoy Steel in Seoul
overnight_items.body_text: National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac held his first meeting with the newly arrived US envoy Steel, according to a ROK official. The meeting is the first confirmed contact between the new US representative and senior ROK national security leadership, occurring against the backdrop of consecutive DPRK SRBM launches and Ulchi Freedom Shield preparations.

overnight_items.headline: Planet Labs imagery: 380+ homes destroyed at DPRK military base near South Korean border
overnight_items.body_text: NK Pro analysis of Planet Labs satellite imagery shows at least 380 duplex-style single-story homes were completely washed away at a North Korean military base close to the South Korean border after a dam appeared to break in late July. No North Korean state media has reported on the flooding or casualties at the facility.

overnight_items.headline: NK Pro imagery: DPRK parade training trucks dispersed — no large-scale parade imminent
overnight_items.body_text: Satellite imagery analysis published by NK Pro shows hundreds of transport trucks for soldiers have disappeared from North Korea's main military parade training base following a small-scale parade late last month, indicating no plans for a large-scale parade in the next few months. The assessment reduces the probability of a major military parade as a provocation mechanism in the near-term Ulchi Freedom Shield window.

overnight_items.headline: WSJ: Pyongyang missile test signals growing conflict between North Korea and US allies
overnight_items.body_text: The Wall Street Journal reports that North Korea's latest missile launches signal an escalating conflict between Pyongyang and US allies, framing the consecutive SRBM tests — coinciding with the Hiroshima anniversary on Aug 6 and Kim Yo Jong's warnings against Japan — as a deliberate signaling campaign. The WSJ contextualizes the launches within Japan's development of counterstrike capabilities and regional military buildup.

overnight_items.headline: Seoul rejects US lawmakers' claim that revised network act discriminates against American firms
overnight_items.body_text: The ROK government rejected claims by US lawmakers that South Korea's revised network act is discriminatory against American technology companies, asserting the law applies on a non-discriminatory basis. The pushback comes as the US-Korea trade relationship is under scrutiny, with Section 301 investigations ongoing and digital services regulation increasingly a bilateral friction point.

also_today.headline: NBR: Digital regulation in Asia — South Korea's outlier approach assessed
also_today.body_text: The National Bureau of Asian Research examines South Korea's distinctive approach to digital regulation in Asia, assessing how Seoul's regulatory framework diverges from regional and US norms. Relevant as the ROK government faces pushback from US lawmakers over the revised network act.

also_today.headline: KEIA: South Korea wants to be a NATO partner, not just a vendor
also_today.body_text: Korea Economic Institute of America argues Seoul seeks a strategic partnership role within the NATO framework rather than simply an arms-supply relationship, as South Korea's defense industry exports to European NATO members have accelerated since 2022.

also_today.headline: Vietnam to build memorial to North Korean war dead outside Hanoi
also_today.body_text: Vietnam will build a memorial at an existing cemetery commemorating 14 North Korean fighter pilots shot down while fighting the US Air Force in the late 1960s, the Diplomat reports. The development underscores DPRK's historical ties with socialist states and comes as Pyongyang's diplomatic footprint with non-allied countries remains limited.

also_today.headline: POSCO Holdings to divest 2.5 trillion won in stakes across 2 affiliates
also_today.body_text: POSCO Holdings announced Friday it will divest approximately 2.5 trillion won worth of shares in two of its affiliates as part of a portfolio restructuring. The move comes as POSCO faces ongoing pressure from 50% US Section 232 steel tariffs with no quota exemption under the current US-Korea trade framework.

also_today.headline: 6 South Korean activists booked over unauthorized Ukraine visit related to North Korean POWs
also_today.body_text: South Korean authorities booked six activists who visited Ukraine in May without government authorization in connection with North Korean prisoners of war held there. The case intersects with ROK-Russia tensions and the ongoing DPRK troop deployment issue in the Russia-Ukraine war.

also_today.headline: South Korea and US sign MOU to expand Korean War veterans affairs cooperation
also_today.body_text: The ROK veterans ministry signed a preliminary agreement with the US to expand cooperation on Korean War veterans affairs, per Yonhap. The MOU formalizes expanded coordination on veteran welfare, remains identification, and commemorative programs for the war's 76th anniversary year.

us_korea_deals.state_of_play: Seoul faces a 10% Section 122 baseline tariff (expired Jul 24; Section 301 now primary vehicle) with steel at 50% and autos at 15%; the $350B investment pledge is 28% fulfilled at $99.1B, with the polysilicon derivatives tariff set at 15% effective Aug 7.

known_deals.company: Samsung Heavy Industries / Vigor Marine Group

trade_policy.detail: Launched Mar 11 2026 against 16 trading partners including South Korea; now the primary legal vehicle for new tariff authority following Section 122 surcharge expiry Jul 24 2026. No completion deadline announced.

trade_policy.item: BIS Semiconductor Export Controls — Samsung and SK Hynix China fabs
trade_policy.detail: Samsung and SK Hynix China fabs operating under annual BIS export licenses renewed Dec 30 2025 for 2026; maintenance and incremental upgrades only, no expansion. Shifted from indefinite VEU waivers to restrictive annual licenses Jan 2026.
Foreign Entity of Concern rules affect Korean EV battery makers (LG Energy Solution, SK On, Samsung SDI) sourcing from China. Phase-in: battery components Dec 2024, critical minerals Dec 2025.

trade_policy.item: CHIPS Act Guardrails — Samsung Taylor TX fabs
trade_policy.detail: Samsung received preliminary $6.4B CHIPS award (Apr 2024) for Taylor TX fabs. 10-year restriction on materially expanding semiconductor manufacturing in countries of concern. Samsung Xi'an NAND fab limited to legacy production under guardrails.

trade_policy.item: Network Act — Digital Services Regulation Dispute
trade_policy.detail: US lawmakers have challenged South Korea's revised network act as discriminatory against American technology firms; ROK government rejected the claims Aug 7, asserting the law is non-discriminatory. USTR monitoring.

deals.headline: Trump imposes 15% tariff on polysilicon derivatives — benefits Korean solar producers in US market
deals.detail: Trump's 15% tariff on polysilicon derivatives, announced Aug 7, effectively advantages Korean producers Hanwha and OCI over Chinese competitors in the US solar supply chain.

business_economy.headline: South Korea overtakes Japan in H1 exports on AI chip boom
business_economy.body_text: South Korea's first-half 2026 exports surpassed Japan's, driven by AI chip demand, per KED Global. The milestone reflects the sustained semiconductor export cycle that also produced a record current account surplus in June.

business_economy.headline: Naver Q2 net income up 41.6% as AI boosts core business
business_economy.body_text: Naver Corp. reported Q2 net income up 41.6%, driven by AI-related growth in its core business, per Yonhap. Naver's AI infrastructure pivot mirrors SK Telecom's data center doubling, reflecting the broader Korean tech sector's reorientation toward AI monetization.

business_economy.headline: SK Telecom accelerates shift to AI infrastructure as data center sales double
business_economy.body_text: SK Telecom reported data center sales doubled as it accelerates its pivot to AI infrastructure, per KED Global. The company's shift positions it alongside Naver in monetizing Korea's AI investment wave.

business_economy.headline: KOGAS Q2 net nearly quadruples on equity gains
business_economy.body_text: Korea Gas Corp. (KOGAS) reported Q2 net income nearly quadrupling, driven by equity gains, per Yonhap. KOGAS is a key party in the US-Korea investment deal energy bucket, committed to purchasing 3.3 million tonnes per annum of US LNG annually.

business_economy.headline: Chinese EV expansion in Latin America threatens Hyundai and Kia market share
business_economy.body_text: Chinese electric vehicle makers are expanding aggressively in Latin America, posing a direct threat to Hyundai and Kia's established market positions in the region, per KED Global. The competitive pressure in Latin America mirrors the Chinese EV challenge Hyundai faces globally as it accelerates its own EV lineup.

northeast_asia.headline: CSIS: Old friends, new calculations — a reset in China–North Korea relations
northeast_asia.body_text: CSIS published analysis of what it characterizes as a reset in China-North Korea relations, examining how Pyongyang is recalibrating its ties with Beijing amid the NK-Russia axis expansion. The analysis is directly relevant to the Korea Chair's current research on the NK-Russia axis and Beijing's tolerance for DPRK provocations.

northeast_asia.headline: How South Korea can survive the unbundling of international order
northeast_asia.body_text: The Diplomat publishes analysis arguing that South Korea's strategic challenges — including fraying multilateral institutions and US alliance uncertainty — require a democratic multilateralism framework. The piece is relevant to ongoing ROK positioning within NATO partnership frameworks and US-ROK-Japan trilateral coordination.

gallup_spotlight.finding: Real estate policy ranks as the top negative evaluation of the Lee Jae-myung administration in its first term, cited by 22% of respondents, with the comprehensive property tax increase debate as the leading specific grievance.

top_articles.headline: North Korea launches short-range ballistic missile toward East Sea: JCS
top_articles.summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed North Korea launched a short-range ballistic missile toward the East Sea on August 6, the second consecutive day of SRBM launches.

top_articles.headline: North Korea fires short-range ballistic missile, South Korea says
top_articles.summary: North Korea launched a short-range ballistic missile on August 6, with state media remaining silent on the test — the second consecutive launch without KCNA acknowledgment.

top_articles.headline: North Koreans urged to beat heat with dog-meat soup
top_articles.summary: KCNA issued guidance urging North Koreans to consume dog-meat soup (boshintang) to cope with a record-breaking summer heatwave, with state media running weeklong heat warnings but reporting no casualties.

kcna_delta.bottom_line: KCNA remained silent on the August 6 SRBM launch for a second consecutive day, continuing the blackout on missile tests while state media focused on the heatwave; Kim Jong Un has not appeared publicly in 10 days with Ulchi Freedom Shield approaching. Watch for a Kim appearance or further provocation — potentially a longer-range launch — in the days before or during the exercise.
